Overview of SGPs and their Use

Damian Betebenner
Center for Assessment

April 30, 2021

Descriptive accountability
• The quality of large-scale summative assessment data collect
today is very high.
• People often conflate large scale assessment and accountability
because the data derived from the assessments often find their
way into state accountability systems but rarely have other uses.
• This is unfortunate as the data has many more uses than just
accountability.
• Goal: Move from seeing data as a hammer (accountability) to
seeing data as a flashlight.

Large scale assessment data
Accountability system results can have value without making causal
inferences about school quality, solely from the results of student
achievement measures and demographic characteristics. Treating the
results as descriptive information and for identification of schools that
require more intensive investigation of organizational and instructional
process characteristics are potentially of considerable value. Rather than
using the results of the accountability system as the sole determiner of
sanctions for schools, they could be used to flag schools that need more
intensive investigation to reach sound conclusions about needed
improvements or judgments about quality
[Linn, 2008, p. 21].

Descriptive accountability
• SGPs are a descriptive growth measure that support both norm- and
criterion-referenced interpretations of student growth.
• SGP are norm-referenced
• Student growth targets (sometimes called adequate growth percentiles) indicate
growth necessary to reach desired achievement outcomes (standards)
• SGPs are individual level that can be aggregated for any group of interest.
• SGPs are uncorrelated with prior achievement. Any student regardless of
where they start, can demonstrate high or low growth.
• Mean/median SGPs (cohort referenced) are 50 for each grade x content area.
• Deviations of mean/median SGPs above/below 50 indicate groups with high/
low growth (i.e. learning) of interest for further investigation.

Four Investigations
• Mean/Median SGP by content area for schools and districts. Which
schools have high/low scores? Why? Are there schools districts with
high/low mean SGPs in one content area but not another?
• Mean/Median SGP by grade within school? Are there schools with large
differences by grade? By content area?
• Mean/Median SGP by demographic subgroup for state? Where are the
largest growth gaps?
• Mean/Median SGP by demographic subgroup for schools and districts?
Are there schools or districts who have closed growth gaps? Are there
schools or districts with especially large growth gaps.

Investigations Associated with Learning Loss
• A large part of our work this year is helping states understand what has
happened to students academically during the pandemic.
• The modus operandi is the same: Descriptive accountability.
• Describe which students, schools, districts demonstrated learning loss
(pandemic related academic impact) in what content area and to what
extent.
• Did student learning differ by mode of education (e.g., remote/hybrid/
in-person)
• Did particular demographic subgroups fare better/worse than others.
